summary.one_liner: ReactAgent is an experimental autonomous agent that uses GPT-4 to generate and compose React components from user stories.
summary.what_it_does: ReactAgent takes a user story written as a markdown file and uses the OpenAI API (GPT-4) to produce React components. The README says the first step converts the user story into a JSON file, and later steps generate the components from it. It can also compose new components from existing ones and use a local design system as input. The generated code targets React, TailwindCSS, TypeScript, Radix UI, and Shadcn UI, and follows Atomic Design principles. The workflow is customized by editing backend/main/react-agent/generateComponents.ts, and a frontend app renders the results. The project is organized as a monorepo with separate backend and frontend parts, started with yarn scripts.
use_cases: generate React components from user stories
compose new components from an existing component library
scaffold Tailwind and Shadcn UI components
notable: Generates React components from a plain-text user story file
Can compose new components from existing components in a local design system
Frontend renders generated components in a sample app, with a JSON skeleton option
caveats: The README says generated code is not production-ready and is for prototyping only.
Requires GPT-4 access; GPT-3.5 is not supported, and GPT-4 token usage can be expensive.
